name: comp-127
title: Directional Pan Controls
description: A small cross-shaped pad of four outlined icon buttons, one per direction, arranged around a plain circle marker. Hovering an arrow lightens its tile; it is made for panning a camera or map.
use: A 3D viewer, map or canvas needs simple four-way nudge buttons rather than drag gestures.
avoid: Only four directions exist, no buttons carry handlers, and diagonal or continuous movement is unsupported.
a11y: Each arrow is labelled by direction and focus is ringed, but no button is wired to any actual movement. (keyboard: yes, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Four dark rounded square buttons with thin outlines form a cross on a near-black stage: a chevron up on top, left and right in the middle row, and down at the bottom. A small white ring sits in the gap at the centre.
behaves: Hovering any arrow brightens its tile and focus rings it; pressing is meant to pan the view that way, but nothing on the pad itself moves or updates.
customise: There are no props: the four directions, their labels and the centre marker are fixed and no handlers are wired, so behaviour means a source edit.
weight: light: Four outlined icon buttons and a centre dot; nothing animates.
issues: Only four directions are offered and none of the buttons has an action attached.
polishWhy: Even, readable d-pad; plain outlined buttons with no working movement.
